build: PAL disk, side 1 OVL1 at its hand-over to $0400

exclude: zero page, the stack and the game's working variables at $0200-$03FF (the score digits, the joystick and the scratch bytes), all written before they are read
the screen, its sprite pointers and the panel, drawn by $38C4, $3BC2 and $3AD4
the music driver's workspace for the three voices and its note-length table, set by $E222 before use
one byte of the waveform command table $E572 that the emulator's memory map marks as run; no jump in the code reaches it
extra: the rest of the 120 room kinds from $3591
the rest of the room kinds' shape lists from $36D3
the rest of the shapes from $37C0
the rest of the 256 character colours from $3C93
sprite shapes, read by the video chip
the ten room maps, read by $3543
the title and jungle character sets, copied to $4800

comments.text: Entry to the jungle confrontation: masks the CIA interrupts, sets the video bank, screen, and charset, points the IRQ at $0EE4 on line $F8, clears the score digits and play variables, starts the section's tune ($E222 with Y=0), places the player at $A0,$78, and shows the section title ($C08F).
Picks the frames, colours, and positions of the two shot sprites for this frame ($0F14 cycles 0-2), using the alternative set while the player throws ($0A4C) or a grenade flies ($17B6).
Player's Y.
Y of each enemy, three slots.
Spare byte after the player's Y position, cleared on each restart.
Player's X.
X of each enemy.
The second enemy's X position.
The enemies' walking step, set each frame by $1D1D.
The player's facing for the walking code at $0906.
Set while each enemy slot is in use.
Cleared on entry to the bunker by $3001.
Five bytes set at the start of the load and not used again.
The pause flag: $0F7D sets it on P and clears it on G, and the main loops at $1CF7 and $3325 wait while it is set.
The grenade's horizontal step, per grenade.
Counts down the grenade's flight.
Mines and tripwires left to place in the room.
Barnes's stage; at 3 he starts shooting back.
Barnes's state: $FF waiting, 1 shooting after three hits.
The grenade's vertical step, per grenade.
Counts down to the sniper's next shot.

Counts frames in Barnes's routine.

Barnes's horizontal step.
Set while the fall finishes.
The enemies' speed, cleared by $11C3.
Barnes's vertical step.

The start of an older version of the player's controls, which nothing in this load calls: the controls in use are read_joystick ($1E32). This part, entered at $0592, puts the standing frames back ($0564, $0F31, $0F32) when the stick is let go, after any wait still counting in $0740.

The older controls, continued. From $0614 they wait for $0303 to be 4, read the joystick into $0306, test the space bar ($08F3), and go on by direction: up to $0694, which starts a jump, down to $06E4, left to $0745 and right to $07C8. $0612 is set while fire is held, which stops the walking; $06E1 and $06E2 hold the jump's step and direction.
The grenade's arc, read by $21A8.
The older controls, continued: left, from $0745, first turns the player to face left (frame $6E), then walks him, stepping the frames from $0851 (or $0855 when $0FAB is 2) every $0FAB frames.
The older controls, continued: the rest of left, then right from $07C8, which does the same with the frames from $0849 (or $084D).
The older controls' right, continued to its rts at $0844.
Counts the player's walking frames left and right.
Counts the walking frames up and down.
Set while the player faces left.
Set while the player faces right.
Where a shot starts across, for each facing.
Where a shot starts down, for each facing.
Horizontal walking steps.
Vertical walking steps.
Walking limits, one for each direction.
Walking limits on the other axis.
Explosion offsets across.
Explosion offsets down.
Explosion frame for each step.
The explosion's sizes and the tables after them.
The older controls' jump, once a frame: steps $06E1 through the 32 heights from $089C into $0581, keeps the jump's direction in $0308, and at the end puts the player back on line $78.

The jump's heights, continued to $08BB, then more heights to $08F2, which the unused enemy routine at $10CC reads from $08C3. From $08F3 the older controls test the space bar, which threw a grenade, and go on into start_throw.

Starts a grenade throw for the older controls, which nothing in this load calls: sets the throwing frames, moves the player $10 pixels left ($10 right when facing left, $0847) and sets the throw flags $0A4C-$0A4E.

Steps the older controls' throw by its counter $0A4C, from 10 to $46: it sets the throwing frames and starts the grenade, goes back to the standing frames at $1E, moves the grenade by throw_arc ($2289) and the steps at $0A4F (or $0A9D facing left), and ends the throw at $46. Nothing in this load calls it: the throw in use is throw_step ($2207).
Set while the throw animation runs.
The walking animation's position.
The walking animation's second counter.
The older throw's steps, one for each count of $0A4C after 10, which it stores in $0575; the steps for facing left start at $0A9D.
The older throw's tables, continued: the steps for facing left from $0A9D, then more steps up to $0B2E that nothing reads.
Raster interrupt at line $14: sets the scroll and charset, places all eight play sprites from $0F15, and overlays the grenade or the dying Barnes ($3078, $3297); chains to $0D78 on line $50.
Self-modified: low byte of the next raster interrupt, written to $FFFE.
Self-modified: high byte of the next raster interrupt, written to $FFFF.
Raster interrupt for the top of the play area: sets the charset and sprite colours, places all eight sprites from $0F15, and in Barnes's bunker or the escape ($3297) shows the extra sprites.
Sprite X high bits for the play area.
Enemy sprite settings, written by $2506.

The invaders' interrupt for their second row, which the top of the screen's interrupt ($0B2F) chains to while they play: points the next interrupt at $0C60 on line row3_y ($2AAE), turns the border red, and places six sprites from $0CE3 with the colours at $0D4E and the frames at $0D66.

The invaders' interrupt for their third row: points the next interrupt at $0CA2 on line row4_y ($2AAF), turns the border cyan, and places six sprites from $0CF3 with the colours at $0D54 and the frames at $0D6C.

The invaders' interrupt for their fourth row: points the next interrupt at the panel's ($0E3B) on line $DC, turns the border purple, and places six sprites from $0D03 with the colours at $0D5A and the frames at $0D72.
X and Y of the six invaders in the second row; both are zero for one that has been shot. The reset at $C024 clears all four rows.
X and Y of the six invaders in the third row.
X and Y of the six invaders in the fourth row.
Where the invaders start: X and Y of the six in the first row, copied to the play sprites at $0F15; from $0D24, 36 bytes copied over the other rows from $0CE3.
The last of the invaders' starting places.
Colours of the first row: orange.
Colours of the second row: white.
Colours of the third row: cyan.
Colours of the fourth row: purple.
Sprite frames of the first row: $FF, the invader's shape.

Sprite frames of the fourth row.
Raster interrupt on line $50: places the player's three sprites ($0F2B-$0F36) and the grenade ($0E36-$0E39), then chains to $0E3B on line $D0.
Raster interrupt lower down: places the player's three-sprite body from $0F2B, and outside the bunker the enemy pair from $0E36; flashes the second sprite white when $03AB is 7.
Grenade X.
Grenade Y.

Y of the grenade's blast.

Raster interrupt at the panel: resets the scroll, charset, and sprites for the status panel, places the crosshair in aiming mode ($03AB=7), cycles $0F14, sets the frame flag $1E24, and chains back to $0EE4.
Raster interrupt on line $F8: plays the music ($C016) and chains to $0B2F.

Set at the start of the load by $04DF.

Run-stop pauses the game ($056F); the unpause key clears it.
Set at the start of the load by $04E9.
Brings an enemy in from the left walking right.
Brings an enemy in from the right walking left.
Two routines like the turns after them, which only the unused routine at $10E0 calls: $101C turns an enemy right and $1032 left, a pixel a step, with frames $44 and $45.
Turns an enemy to walk right, unless they are frozen ($115C).
Turns an enemy to walk left.
Enter from the left at double speed.
Enter from the right at double speed.

Enemy routines that nothing in this load calls: they bring an enemy in standing on line $46 ($1098, $10A9) or held still on line $64 ($10FC, $110A), start and step a jump by the heights at $08C3 ($10BA, $10CC), end the jump on line $78 facing the player ($10E0), and start and step a second kind of jump by the heights at $089C ($1118, $1131).
Set for an enemy that the unused routines from $10FC hold still or move through a jump; the turns at $1048 and $1067 leave such an enemy alone.
An unused routine that crouches an enemy: frame $54, or $9A facing left, with a second sprite 20 lines under it.
The crouch, continued, then from $119E an unused routine that stands an enemy still with frame $4D.
Clears an enemy that has walked out, past X $50, or below 5 when its state ($0F26) is 0, by running on into clear_enemy; nothing calls this entry.
Clears an enemy slot.

An unused routine that fires a shot from an enemy into the first free of two shot slots ($0F3A, $0F3B), ten lines lower when the enemy crouches. $1245 makes an enemy crouch and fire, or fire and jump, and from $1264 counts $1280 down to turn the enemy towards the player ($1270). Only the unused engine at $12AC names them.
Which way each enemy faces, 1 right or 2 left, set by the turns at $1048 and $1067 and read only by routines nothing in this load calls.
Four scripts of ten steps for the unused engine at $12AC, at $1284, $128E, $1298 and $12A2; each step is a number in its routine table at $130E.

An engine that steps each enemy through a script, which nothing in this load calls: every 16 calls ($1300) it takes the enemy's next step from its script (chosen by $1302 through $1306), and calls the routine the step names in $130E by rewriting the jump at $12F8.
The script engine, continued.
Each enemy's step in its script, 0-8, for the unused engine at $12AC; the entries at $0FAC and $0FE4 clear it.
Each enemy's script for the unused engine at $12AC, set to 1 by the entries at $0FAC and $0FE4; from $1306 the scripts' addresses, and from $130E the addresses of the routines a step can name.

A jump on to $13BB, then from $1329 an unused routine that steps an enemy's walking frames from the tables at $0849-$0858 every seven calls, leaving alone an enemy whose frame is $54, $56, $9A or $9C.
The enemy walking routine, continued, to $13BC; $13BD-$13C2 are its counters.

Two unused routines that climb the player: while $1441 is set, $13C3 moves him up four lines every ten calls with the frames at $143D, and while $1442 is set, $1402 moves him down. The older controls' standing code ($059D) leaves the frames alone while either is set.
Checks the player against each enemy and each enemy shot, and against the grenade's blast; any contact kills the player ($3B17, $1519).
Frames left of the player's death, from $50.
Starts the player's death: stops the shots, sets the timer, and plays the death sound.
Steps the death animation by $1518 (falling frames at $4E, $46, $3C, $32); at the end clears the shots and takes a life ($15ED), restarting at $3396, or with Barnes dead ends the section ($34F6).
A second rts that nothing reaches.
Sets the player's three body frames to the standing pose $56.
Sets the player's three body frames to the pose $6E, as stand_frames does for $56; nothing calls it.
Moves the player's body frames on three to the next walking pose.
Moves the player's body frames on three for the other walking direction.
Sets the crouching frames $61, $5F and $60.
Clears the shots, then either takes the next wound through $34F6 or, with no wounds left, empties the morale bar, drops a life from $C08D and restarts the jungle at $3396.
Ends the hit test when the shot slot is empty.
Tests each of the three shots against each enemy; a hit kills the enemy through $16A9 and scores 500.
Self-modified: the hit box's left margin, set at $1BE5.
Self-modified: the hit box's right margin.
Self-modified: the hit box's top margin.
Self-modified: the hit box's bottom margin.
Self-modified: the horizontal margin on one side.
Self-modified: the horizontal margin on the other side, then the kill: five calls to $3AA7 add 500, and a grenade from $28C3 explodes.
Steps to the next enemy and the next shot.
Drops the return address and goes on to the next enemy.
Frames left of each enemy's death, 0 when alive.
Hits on Barnes, who falls at the fifth.
An enemy is hit: plays the sound, starts their death ($16A3=$28) and stops them. When the enemy is Barnes ($3078), each throw-time hit counts, and the fifth ends him ($3227).
Set once Barnes has been hit by the current shot.
Barnes is beaten: clears $16A8, removes him through $11BE and goes to $3227.
An rts after the jump to barnes_killed, which nothing reaches.
Plays the falling sound and starts the enemy's 40-frame fall in $16A3.
Steps each dying enemy: the fallen frames at $26 and the slot cleared at 2.
Checks the four ground characters under the player: a mine (characters 7-$0B) explodes ($175A), and a trap ($0C-$10) catches him ($17B7).
A mine goes off under the player: plays the blast, starts the explosion sprite at the mine ($17B6), clears the mine from the map, and kills the player.
Frames left of a mine's explosion.
The player falls into a trap: flags it ($17C4) and kills him.
Set when the player died in a trap.
Steps the mine explosion's frames and size by $17B6.
Offsets of the four map characters under the player's feet.
X offset of the explosion for each foot.
Y offset of the explosion for each foot.

An older map scroller, which nothing in this load calls. It moves the map pointer at $20/$21, where the scroller in use moves zp32-35 ($2070): $1831 and $184C step it one character right or left every eight pixels ($0309), and $1869 and $1889 a row down or up every six ($030A).
The older scroller, continued. From $18AB it draws fifteen blocks of the map from $20/$21 onto the screen at $4000 and their colours, stepping by the tables from $19B5.
Fills both screens ($4000 and $4400) with spaces and the colours with white.
An unused routine that copies 159 bytes from $1B5D onto the screen at $4320 as characters, in white.
Multiplies X (low) and Y (high) by A into $0398/$0399; only the invaders ($28E2) call it, to find a screen row.
Tests the key with matrix code A; sets carry when that key alone is held.
Saved Y of the key test.
Keyboard row masks.
Keyboard column masks.
Counts the time limit down once a second ($1B5C counts $32 frames): four digits, minutes and seconds.
Draws the four time digits on the panel.
Time left: tens of minutes, minutes, tens of seconds, and seconds.
Minutes digit of the time limit.
Tens of seconds of the time limit.
Seconds of the time limit.
Frames until the next second.

Start of play: starts the section's tune, copies the jungle charset from $A800 to $4800, clears the shots and enemies, sets the time to 20 minutes, sets the enemy speed operands and the panel, draws the jungle ($3543), and enters the main loop.
Self-modified: low byte of the charset source.
Self-modified: high byte of the charset source, stepped each page.
Self-modified: low byte of the charset destination.
Copies the charset from $A800 to $4800, then sets everything for a new start: the time 02:00, the hit box, the first room $69, the colours, ammunition 9, four wounds, morale $47, and the panel.
Restart after a lost life: redraws the map and panel ($3634, $3BC2, $38C4, $3AD4), resets Barnes's state, picks how many enemies come ($1E27), and runs the main loop.

Main loop, once per frame flag $1E24: pause, the player's joystick ($1E32) and hit checks, the time limit (at zero a life is lost), and the updates of enemies, shots, grenades, Barnes, the mines, and the music keys.
When five keys are held together, flashes the border and sets the game to end.
The music key turns the tune on and the effects key turns it off.
Set by the panel interrupt each frame.
Index into $1E27, stepped each life.
How many enemies come in each wave.

Reads the joystick: up and down move the player along the jungle path ($1FE3, $2070), left and right ($1EBE, $1F1F) where the map's characters allow, fire throws ($20FD); standing still shows the standing frames.
Acts on the joystick in $0306: left, right, up, down, and fire at $20FD; when standing still the body shows facing left or right.
Moves the player right one step if the map ahead is clear, scrolling the map pointer a row every eight pixels.
Moves the player left one step if the map allows and the edge is not reached.
Fine scroll of the player's position, 0-7.
Fine horizontal position, 0-7.
Slows the player's walking.
Written by $351C on a room change.
Steps the walking frames every fourth call; returns to the caller's caller between steps.
Steps walk_count_b round, wrapping at 3, and runs on into no_move, like the end of step_animation; nothing jumps to this entry.
Returns without moving.
Moves the player up the screen where the map allows.
Set where the path above is blocked to enemies and player.
Set where the path below is blocked.
Moves the player down the screen where the map allows, scrolling the map pointers zp32/33 and zp34/35 a column every eight pixels.

Fire shoots: if rounds are left ($3B15) and a shot slot is free, uses a round ($3AE8) and starts a shot ($213E); once the player has reached Barnes's bunker ($307C) it throws a grenade instead ($21C8).
Starts shot X from the player's gun with the gunfire sound: works out its slope towards the screen's centre line ($25E1/$25EF) and sends it up the screen.
Frames before the next shot.
Throws a grenade at the enemy in the last stage: uses shot slot 2 on a higher arc and starts the throw animation ($0A4C=$50).
Steps the grenade throw by $0A4C: the arm frames, the grenade's rise, the explosion sound at $1A, and the end at 1.
Height change of the grenade for each step of the throw.
The rest of throw_arc's heights: falling three pixels a step.

Every $C8 frames, unless one is in the air, a sniper's shot (or thrown object) comes in from one of fifteen places ($239A, $23BC) and falls for eight steps, then bursts where it lands ($0E38) with a sound.
Which place the next sniper shot comes from, 0-14.
Steps left of the falling shot.
Frames until the next sniper shot.
Sprite frame of the falling shot.
Colour of the falling shot, cycled.
X and Y where each sniper shot starts.
Each enemy's colour.
X drift of each sniper shot.
The last of twenty steps from $23E9, five of 3 and five of -3 in turn.
An enemy fires at the player: finds a free enemy-shot slot, plays the sound, and aims the shot at the player's position from the enemy's ($2445).
A jump to barnes_fires ($307D) and an rts after the rts above, which nothing reaches.
Plays the grenade's sounds: two effects in the jungle, one in the bunker.
Aims enemy shot Y from enemy X at the player: slope and direction in $0573/$057A and $25E4/$25F2.
Frames before each enemy can fire again.
Written on entry to the bunker.
Applies this frame's movement: the player within the screen's edges (with the X high bit), the two enemies, and every shot along its slope, and drifts the blast.
Slope step of each shot.
Horizontal distance from enemy to player for each enemy shot.
Running sum of each shot's slope.
Cleared when an enemy shot starts.
Divisor of each shot's slope.
Vertical distance for each enemy shot.

Copies the player's and enemies' positions into the sprite table, three sprites each, and picks the player's frames for his height on screen (lower rows use frames $40 further on, for the jungle's foreground).
Counts down the fire delay and removes shots that leave the screen; removes a blast that leaves the play area.
Clears shot X.
A second rts after the one above, which nothing reaches.
Steps each enemy: walking frames every fourth frame, a shot at the player every fifteenth ($23FD), turning back at the blocked edges ($1048, $1067), and leaving at the sides.
Frames to each enemy's next walking frame.
Walking frame of each enemy, 0-3.
Frames to each enemy's next shot.
An empty routine.

While enemies remain in this wave ($28C3) and the player is in the lower half, brings a new enemy into each empty slot after a random delay (from the bytes at $0400), from the left or right side the path allows.
Running sum that brings each enemy in when it passes $FA.
Index into the random bytes, 0-$13.
Second random index, 0-$1D.
Enemies still to come in this wave.
Which side each random step brings an enemy from.

A game of Space Invaders, which nothing in Platoon starts. It clears the screens, sets mode 7 ($03AB) so that the panel's interrupt shows the gun and marks each frame, draws three shields from $2F55, and sets up four rows of six invaders: the first row in the play sprites at $0F15, the others at $0CE3, $0CF3 and $0D03 for the interrupts at $0C1E, $0C60 and $0CA2.

Puts the rows at the top, on lines $37, $50, $69 and $82 (row1_y-row4_y), marching right a step every $14 frames, with the gun at $8C,$E1, and chains the top of the screen's interrupt to $0C1E. The rows come back here when the top row has come down to line $6E.

The main loop, once a frame: reads the joystick ($2B17), moves the shot ($2B89) and shows it in sprite 7, drops bombs ($2CD6), and starts the rows at the top again once they have come down far enough.
Every march_delay frames the rows step four pixels sideways ($2AB1, $2AE4); when an invader reaches either edge they turn and come down four lines.

Each invader's Y follows its row; then the shot is tested against the invaders ($2BA9), the bombs against the gun ($2F0D) and the shot against the shields ($2EC6), the bombs fall ($2E4F), and the quit key is checked ($C059).
Frames between the rows' steps: $14 at the start, one or two fewer for each invader shot.
Counts the frames up to march_delay.
Set once a frame by the panel's interrupt ($0E9E) while the invaders play; their main loop waits for it.
X of the invaders' gun, 24-250.
Y of the invaders' gun, line $E1.
Line of the invaders' first row.
Line of the invaders' second row, where the top interrupt chains to $0C1E.
Line of the invaders' third row.
Line of the invaders' fourth row.
Which way the rows march: 1 right, $FF left.
Moves every live invader four pixels right.
Moves every live invader four pixels left.
Reads the joystick for the invaders: left and right move the gun between 24 and 250, fire shoots when no shot is in the air.
Moves the shot up four lines a frame, and ends it above line $32.
X of the gun's shot.
Y of the gun's shot, 0 when there is none.
The shot's step, -4.
Tests the shot against each invader, five lines and nine pixels either way: one hit is cleared from its row, counted, and the march speeds up. When all 24 are shot the game starts again at $28E2.
Invaders shot so far.
Clears the shot.
All 24 shot: drops the return address and starts again.
Every six frames picks the next of 25 invaders in turn from bomb_slots and bomb_rows, and if it is still there puts a bomb, character $0F, on the screen under it.
Counts the frames between bombs.
The invader whose turn it is to bomb.
The step through the 25 turns.
Which invader of its row each turn picks.
Which row each turn picks, 0-3.
Finds the screen place under the picked invader of the first row, and from $2D96, $2DD6 and $2E0F under one of the other rows, then puts the bomb there ($2E48).
Cleared when the picked invader has been shot.
The same for an invader of the third row, and from $2E0F of the fourth.
Puts the bomb character $0F on the screen at the address written into this instruction.
The invader's screen column.
Every ten frames moves each bomb on the screen down a row: a bomb landing on a shield wears it from character 2 to 1, then away, and the bottom row is cleared.
Counts the frames between bomb moves.
A bomb found: it leaves its place and moves down a row, wearing away a shield character it lands on, or vanishing at the bottom.
Tests the shot against the shields: a hit wears the shield away a step and ends the shot.
Looks for a bomb in the six character places around the gun ($2F4F); a hit starts the game again at $28E2.
An rts nothing reaches, then the six places around the gun that gun_hit tests: 0, 1, 2, 40, 41 and 42 characters on.
The three shields, three rows of 40 characters copied to the screen at $42D0.
